subject: Severe production throughput & latency spike — NovaLink (exec + ops coordination)
messages:
From: Sally Chen <sally.chen@novalink.io>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: supportops@novalink.io
Date: 2026-09-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Severe throughput and latency spike affecting production

Hannah —

We started seeing a major regression on our production tenant around 08:50 PDT. Token throughput dropped ~70% and 95th percentile latency for short chat requests jumped from ~150ms to ~1.8s. Error rate (5xx) rose from 0.1% to 3.6%. This is impacting several of our customer-facing flows (search, real-time suggestions).

Attached is a screenshot from our observability dashboard showing the spike and one sample trace. We opened a local ticket with our SREs (INC-1129) but we need Redwood to confirm whether this is an agent-side problem or something upstream.

Can we get an immediate point person and an estimate for when this will be stabilized? We're already throttling traffic but that degrades user experience.

Thanks —
Sally Chen
Director of Product
NovaLink Health

Attachment: novalink_slowpath_screenshot.png (image/png, 320KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com
Cc: Sally Chen <sally.chen@novalink.io>
Date: 2026-09-20T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Severe throughput and latency spike affecting production

Team — urgent. Sally reports a cross-tenant throughput collapse + elevated 5xxs for NovaLink production. They are customer-impacting and asking for a point person and ETA.

Immediate asks:
- Marcus: can your team pull the last 30m of router + KV cache telemetry and share a trimmed logs bundle (redwood-internal) to the bridge? Prefer CSV + sample raw logs.
- Rishi: please assess recent rollout/route changes (last 48h) and confirm if any model switch or kernel selection change could explain a slow-path increase.
- Monica: draft an initial customer-facing comm (2-3 lines, empathic + next steps) and a one-page MAP for execs.
- David: evaluate capacity bump/fallback to B-tier models and estimate cost & latency delta.

I've spun up a Zoom bridge: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210 (passcode on Slack). Created JIRA SUP-2138 and put NovaLink as P1. Attachments requested: telemetry snapshot, trimmed logs.

We should meet on the bridge in 10 minutes. If any critical blockers, call me directly.

Hannah
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com, Sally Chen <sally.chen@novalink.io>
Date: 2026-09-20T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Severe throughput and latency spike affecting production

Quick triage from infra: we see a sharp increase in long-tail token latencies that correlate with an unusual spike in cache miss ratio on the regional KV tier serving NovaLink. Initial hypothesis: a mis-eviction pattern in the prefix cache after a high churn event around 08:44 PDT that pushed more requests to slow-path execution.

What I pushed to the bridge:
- novalink-telemetry-snapshot-20260920.csv (sampled counters by backend/service, 08:30-09:30)
- initial-logs-trimmed.txt (router + executor stack frames, 2MB)

Immediate mitigations in progress:
- Rehydrate prefix cache from warm snapshot (2-3 min expected but dependent on IO bandwidth).
- Force-route NovaLink traffic to a healthy pool in us-west-2 while we monitor if miss ratio returns to baseline.

If rehydrate completes and miss ratio drops, that should bring 95th back down rapidly. If not, we escalate to kernel/quantization path analysis.

Marcus
Director, Serving Runtime
Attachment: novalink-telemetry-snapshot-20260920.csv (text/csv, 180KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sally Chen <sally.chen@novalink.io>, marcus.lin@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Severe throughput and latency spike affecting production — executive summary and next steps

Sally / NovaLink team — brief executive summary and commitments from Redwood. Thank you for joining the bridge.

What happened (summary):
- At ~08:44 PDT we observed a high-churn event that caused an elevated KV prefix-cache miss ratio for NovaLink. That in turn pushed more requests into a slower execution path which increased 95th percentile latency and produced higher 5xx rates.

Immediate actions taken:
- Rehydrated prefix cache from warm snapshot; miss ratio dropped 85% within 3 minutes.
- Temporarily routed NovaLink traffic to an alternate healthy pool in us-west-2 to blunt user impact.
- Scoped and uploaded trimmed logs and telemetry to SUP-2138.

Current status:
- 95th latency back to ~210ms (down from 1.8s). Error rate stabilized near baseline; monitoring for regressions.

Next steps and timelines:
- Engineering will run a targeted rehearsal of the cache eviction policy and add a short-term guard (rate-limiter for rehydration storms) by EOD PT.
- Product/Customer Success (Monica) will finalize the customer-facing summary and post-incident report within 24 hours.
- We propose one day of service credit if impacts exceed 90 minutes; Monica will coordinate legal/commercial follow-up.

Open items (owners):
- Rishi: post-mortem on kernel selection and recent rollout artifacts (24–48h).
- Marcus: propose a hardened warm-snapshot cadence and automated prefetch heuristics (72h proposal).
- David: cost estimate for sustained fallback pool (today, within 2 hours).

We will send a formal post-incident report and share any preventive changes in a follow-up. Thank you for the rapid coordination — we appreciate NovaLink's patience.

Hannah Schmitt
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
